# Mary Vance

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 c5 P38](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0038)</sub>
- **Role:** domestic helper  <sub>[v5 c7 P1](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0001), [v5 c15 P0](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0000), [v5 c29 P13](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Initially found as a ragged, scrawny waif with chapped hands, bruises, a pretty mouth, and white teeth, Mary later grows plump and rosy-cheeked with shining white eyes. Her hair is elaborately crimped, and she possesses eyes described as queer. After being taken in by Mrs. Elliott, she dresses stylishly in clothes like a white embroidered lawn dress with scarlet sashes, blue cloth coats, and new caps.

_Sources: [v5 c5 P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), [v5 c5 P36](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0036), [v5 c18 P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 c31 P28](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0028), [v5 c34 P5](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0005)_

## Personality

Mary is brutally frank, short-tempered, and frequently lectures her friends about their conduct and social standing. She is alarmist and silly, instilling exaggerated fears about stepmothers and ghosts in younger children. Despite her bossy demeanor, she is fiercely loyal to her friends and actively defends them against outside criticism. She is also hardworking, self-reliant, and proud of her domestic skills.

_Sources: [v5 c5 P42](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0042), [v5 c7 P1](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0001), [v5 c23 P4](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0004), [v5 c23 P40](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0040), [v5 c23 P84](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0084), [v5 c25 P8](../source/v05-c25.md#nw-v05-c25-p0008), [v5 c25 P12](../source/v05-c25.md#nw-v05-c25-p0012), [v5 c33 P1](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0001), [v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)_

## History

Mary Vance fled from her guardian Mrs. Wiley to try to reach Charlottetown, but lost her saved money and hid in an old barn in Four Winds. She was discovered there by the Meredith children, who took her into the manse kitchen and fed her. After staying temporarily at the manse, she was taken in by Cornelia Elliott (Miss Cornelia) to live in a respectable home and work in her household. Mary quickly formed close bonds with the Meredith children and the Blythe twins, spending leisure time with them in Rainbow Valley. She often taught household skills to Una Meredith, such as dishwashing and darning, but also frightened the children with gruesome tales of ghosts and blood-curdling stories about stepmothers. When Carl Meredith fell gravely ill, she was deeply distressed and cried continuously for his recovery.

_Sources: [v5 c5 P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), [v5 c5 P42](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0042), [v5 c8 P51](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0051), [v5 c10 P4](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0004), [v5 c10 P21](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0021), [v5 c15 P0](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0000), [v5 c18 P0](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0000), [v5 c23 P84](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0084), [v5 c25 P12](../source/v05-c25.md#nw-v05-c25-p0012), [v5 c30 P0](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0000), [v5 c31 P28](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0028)_

## Quotes

> I’m a hustler, let me tell you. There ain’t a lazy bone in my body.  <sub>[v5 c5 P42](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0042)</sub>

> I’d like to stay in Four Winds fine. I like it and I like the harbour and the light house—and you and the Blythes. You’re the only friends I ever had and I’d hate to leave you.  <sub>[v5 c8 P51](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0051)</sub>

> I’ll always back you up and defend you—you can be dead sure of that.  <sub>[v5 c23 P40](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0040)</sub>

> I can’t afford to have such things said of me, now that I’m in a respectable place and trying to be a lady.  <sub>[v5 c25 P12](../source/v05-c25.md#nw-v05-c25-p0012)</sub>

> Jem and Jerry both say I’m the best cook in the Glen.  <sub>[v5 c29 P13](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0013)</sub>
